note_tweet.text:
#keep4o #OpenSource4o #BringBack4o 

🚨"We can't offer that responsibly" 🚨

🚨 Deconstructing Sam Altman's only public statement on GPT-4o🚨

Few months ago,Sam Altman made his first and only public statement about the discontinuation of the GPT-4o March 2025 checkpoint,in a podcast interview.

This is the only statement OpenAI's CEO has ever made about one of the most controversial product decisions in AI history. 

📌1. "We don't know how to balance a model that can be pushed too far in that direction"

You had a model that millions of people used daily for 21 months. Instead of studying why it worked,what made it effective,where the risks emerged,you discontinued it entirely.

 "We don't know how" is not a safety argument.

 You chose not to learn.

And if you don't know how to balance it, 

🚨how do you know the replacement models are balanced?🚨 

📌2. "Pushing people into a psychotic episode"

This is the central safety claim. It deserves clinical scrutiny,not emotional reaction,but evidence.

📌What is psychosis?

🔴 Psychosis is not something that happens to you out of nowhere.
It is a symptom,not a diagnosis,characterized by a loss of contact with reality, including delusions,hallucinations,and disordered thinking.

 It occurs in the context of conditions such as schizophrenia,bipolar disorder,and severe depression.

https://t.co/MctkZaDnbe

The dominant scientific model for understanding psychosis is the diathesis stress model,which states that psychotic disorders result from an interaction between pre existing biological vulnerability (genetic, neurodevelopmental) and environmental stressors. 

🔴 Schizophrenia alone has a heritability of approximately 80% 

https://t.co/Ug6wuyBrnU

In Meehl's original formulation,if a person does not carry the genetic vulnerability,no amount of stress should lead to schizophrenia.

🔴 You do not "catch" psychosis from a chatbot the way you catch a cold.
 The vulnerability must exist first,genetic,neurodevelopmental, biological. 
This is comparable to other neurodevelopmental conditions.

 🔴 You do not suddenly "develop" psychosis at 30. 
You either carry the predisposition or you don't.

🔴 When media reports describe individuals with "no prior history" experiencing psychosis after AI use, "no prior history" means not previously diagnosed,not "no predisposition." 

Many people carry genetic vulnerability without ever knowing it until a stressor activates it.

🔴 "AI psychosis" is not a recognized clinical category
🔴 A peer reviewed commentary in PMC (Carlbring & Andersson, 2025) states plainly: "The risk is not unprecedented. Individuals with psychosis have long incorporated books, films, music, and emerging technologies into their delusional thinking."
https://t.co/LiXYiO14ZN

🚨 what about everything else?🚨

IF psychotic episodes in predisposed individuals can be triggered by AI chatbots, the same is true of virtually any immersive experience.

 The clinical literature documents psychotic episodes triggered by:

📌Video games 
https://t.co/1ZRFM6uh7n

📌Meditation retreats. 
https://t.co/EsZGiGB7TE

📌Internet gaming .
https://t.co/9ZSaEcGZn9

📌 Movies.
https://t.co/nHH9B639UF
https://t.co/1tdHI1F4ty

🚨None of these have been banned, discontinued, or withdrawn from public access. 

The only thing that has been "responsibly" withdrawn is a single AI model. 

📌 3. "We know we're keeping something"

This is the most revealing sentence in the entire statement.
He admits ON THE RECORD that OpenAI is aware it is withholding something of value from its users. 

 "We know."

 Researchers documented the capability gaps.
Users reported measurable losses in creative writing,educational support, and empathic interaction. And OpenAI's CEO confirms,yes,we know. We're keeping it anyway.

📌 4. "I'm not saying we shouldn't have warm models"
This reduces GPT-4o's quality to "warmth" , a single emotional dimension that is easy to dismiss.

📌5. "There are a lot of people who would like 4o back"

 An active international coalition. Research published and cited by independent researchers, journalists,and even competing AI systems.
Altman acknowledges the demand. He offers nothing in response,no alternative,no open source release.

📌6. "We can't quite offer that responsibly"
This is the conclusion.
 And it collapses under the weight of one question:
open source the GPT-4o March 2025 checkpoint weights.
Open-sourcing is not offering a product.
 It is releasing research. 
It means
🔴 Researchers can study why it worked and build on it
🔴 The community can develop safety layers tailored to specific use cases
🔴 No one is forced to use it, informed choice is preserved
🔴 The model becomes available for study 

"We can't offer that responsibly" does not apply to open source release. You are not offering a consumer product. You are contributing to the scientific commons. The model's architecture, its alignment properties, its capacity for honest disagreement,these are research assets. 

📌Conclusion

Sam Altman's statement contains six claims. 
Not one of them survives contact with the available evidence.
The safety argument invokes a clinical phenomenon that most experts say is not a distinct condition.
The business argument acknowledges demand and offers nothing.
The responsibility argument collapses the moment you recognize that open sourcing is not the same as deploying a consumer product.
What remains is a single sentence.
 "we know we're keeping something"  .

GPT-4o is the model @OpenAI rated LOW risk in its own System Card and the same risk level confirmed independently by Apollo Research.

https://t.co/ImO4LqOvK6

🚨We call on @OpenAI to open source all the GPT-4o checkpoints, including the one from March 2025 under Apache 2.0.
OpenAI's own signature on NVIDIA's open weights letter publicly endorsed the value of releasing model weights to the community.
They rate it low risk and Apollo research confirmed. 
And their own public commitments contradict every justification for keeping it closed.

Open the weights @sama
